poster_title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
authors: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, Boyuan Ma, Fenglu Hong, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Jay Rainton, Chen Wu, Mengmeng Ji, Hanchen Li, Urmish Thakker, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun
paper_info: Accepted at International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)

panels.headline: Context adaptation for LLMs without altering weights
content: Context adaptation modifies inputs to large language models (LLMs) to improve model behavior.
Current methods leverage natural language feedback for iterative context adaptation.
Monolithic rewriting by LLMs can lead to context collapse and brevity bias.
ACE framework aims to prevent these issues through structured, incremental updates.
Proposed solution for scalable, efficient, and self-improving LLM systems.

panels.headline: Context collapse and brevity bias
content: Monolithic rewriting by LLMs results in shorter, less informative summaries.
Performance declines due to loss of domain-specific insights and tools.
ACE addresses these challenges by evolving comprehensive contexts.
panels.figure_caption: Figure 2: Context Collapse. Monolithic rewriting of context by an LLM can collapse it into shorter, less informative summaries, leading to sharp performance drops.

panels.headline: ACE framework with three roles: Generator, Reflector, and Curator
content: ACE treats contexts as evolving playbooks that accumulate, refine, and organize strategies over time.
Modular workflow of generation, reflection, and curation guided by a grow-and-refine principle.
Framework includes three roles: Generator, Reflector, and Curator, mirroring human learning processes.
ACE-generated contexts contain detailed, domain-specific insights along with tools and code.
panels.figure_caption: Figure 4: The ACE Framework. Inspired by Dynamic Cheatsheet, ACE adopts an agentic architecture with three specialized components: a Generator, a Reflector, and a Curator.

panels.headline: Evaluated on agent tasks and domain-specific benchmarks
content: ACE framework evaluated on agent tasks and domain-specific benchmarks, particularly financial analysis.
Compared with strong baselines in both offline and online adaptation settings.
Achieved significant improvements in performance and efficiency.
panels.figure_caption: Table 1: Results on the AppWorld Agent Benchmark. "GT labels" indicates whether ground-truth labels are available to the Reflector during adaptation. We evaluate the ACE framework against multiple baselines on top of the official ReAct implementation, both for offline and online context adaptation.

panels.headline: ACE outperformed strong baselines by 10.6% on agents and 8.6% on domain-specific benchmarks
content: ACE outperformed strong baselines by 10.6% on agents and 8.6% on domain-specific benchmarks.
Achieved 86.9% lower adaptation latency and significantly reduced rollout costs.
Matched the top-ranked production-level agent IBMCUGA on average and surpassed it on the harder test-challenge split using a smaller open-source model (DeepSeek-V3.1).
panels.figure_caption: Figure 1: Overall Performance Results. Our proposed framework, ACE, consistently outperforms strong baselines across agent and domain-specific reasoning tasks.

panels.headline: Comprehensive, evolving contexts enable scalable, efficient, and self-improving LLM systems
content: Comprehensive, evolving contexts enable scalable, efficient, and self-improving LLM systems with low overhead.
ACE provides a robust solution to the limitations of existing context adaptation methods, improving performance in knowledge-intensive applications.
ACE framework prevents context collapse and brevity bias through structured, incremental updates.
Demonstrated effectiveness in both offline and online settings, achieving high accuracy and low overhead.
ACE may still face challenges in extremely resource-constrained environments.
